one_liner: Implement a Muon+AdamW hybrid optimizer with MuonClip/QK-clip and a WSD schedule.

key_terms.definition: Optimizer that orthogonalizes the momentum update of 2D weight matrices via Newton-Schulz iterations, pushing equally along every singular direction.
Matmul-only matrix polynomial recurrence that approximates a matrix's orthogonal polar factor UV^T, avoiding an explicit SVD each step.
Adaptive optimizer with decoupled weight decay; here it handles the tied embedding, RMSNorm gains, and all 1D parameters instead of Muon.
Post-step rescaling of a head's query and key weights that caps the maximum pre-softmax attention logit at a threshold tau, preventing blow-ups.
Three-phase learning-rate schedule (linear warmup, constant peak, 1-sqrt decay) with no baked-in total step count, unlike cosine annealing.
Factor 0.2*sqrt(max(m,n)) multiplying Muon's orthogonalized update so its magnitude matches AdamW's, letting one learning rate govern both optimizers.
Attention variant where multiple query heads share fewer key/value heads, requiring QK-clip to scale each shared key slice only once per group.
Token-budget threshold beyond which enlarging the batch yields diminishing returns per step, used to justify the ~0.5M-token effective batch.
Summing gradients over several micro-batches before one optimizer step, used to reach a large effective batch without exceeding GPU memory.
Full matrix-preconditioner optimizer that Muon cheaply approximates via orthogonalization, without forming or inverting the preconditioner.

prerequisites: the attention mechanism and grouped-query attention
